summary.text: Robert C. "Bobby" Scott is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative for Virginia's 3rd District, in office since 1993. A Newport News attorney by training, he served in the Virginia House of Delegates and Virginia Senate before Congress and is the ranking member of the House Education and Workforce Committee.

paragraphs.text: Born in Washington, D.C. in 1947 and grew up in Newport News, Virginia; graduated from Groton School in 1965.
Earned a bachelor's degree in political science from Harvard University in 1969 and a J.D. from Boston College School of Law in 1973.
Served in the U.S. Army Reserve (1970-1974) and the Massachusetts National Guard (1974-1976).
Worked as an attorney in private practice in Newport News from 1973 to 1991.
Elected to the Virginia House of Delegates in 1977, serving until 1983, then to the Virginia Senate, serving until 1993.
Lost his first race for Congress in 1986, in the 1st District, to Republican incumbent Herb Bateman, 56% to 44%.

Elected to the U.S. House in 1992 from the newly created 3rd District and has served since 1993; Wikipedia describes him as the first African American representative from Virginia since Reconstruction and the dean of Virginia's congressional delegation.
Serves on the House Committee on Education and the Workforce, where he is the ranking member; Democratic colleagues elected him ranking member in December 2022.
